name: Enterprise Wireless Security Assessment
description: Ability to assess enterprise wireless deployments including 802.1X/EAP authentication, RADIUS infrastructure, certificate validation, wireless intrusion detection/prevention systems, and network segmentation. Covers attacks against EAP-PEAP, EAP-TLS, EAP-TTLS, and RADIUS server misconfigurations, as well as assessment of wireless management plane security.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to enterprise wireless security assessment

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands enterprise wireless architecture, 802.1X, and EAP authentication methods
evidence: Can describe 802.1X architecture (supplicant, authenticator, authentication server)
Understands the differences between EAP-PEAP, EAP-TLS, and EAP-TTLS
Completed training on enterprise wireless security assessment

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Performs enterprise wireless assessment tasks using standard tools under supervision
evidence: Deployed evil twin attacks against EAP-PEAP networks using hostapd-mana or eaphammer under guidance
Captured EAP credentials from misconfigured supplicants in lab exercises
Assessed wireless controller configurations for common misconfigurations under supervision

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses enterprise wireless deployments end to end
evidence: Independently assessed 3+ enterprise wireless deployments covering authentication, segmentation, and WIDS
Identified certificate validation failures and EAP credential exposure in real engagements
Evaluated RADIUS server configurations and authentication policy enforcement
Produced comprehensive reports with risk-rated findings and remediation roadmaps

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Assesses complex enterprise wireless environments; develops advanced attack chains
evidence: Chained wireless access with internal network pivoting in enterprise assessments
Assessed wireless deployments with WIPS and performed evasion techniques
Evaluated 802.11w (PMF/MFP) and 802.11r (FT) security in enterprise environments
Reviews enterprise wireless assessment reports and mentors junior assessors

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines enterprise wireless assessment methodology; advises on secure architecture design
evidence: Authored the lab's enterprise wireless assessment methodology
Advises clients on enterprise wireless architecture design and hardening
Published research on enterprise 802.1X or EAP security vulnerabilities
Trains teams on enterprise wireless security assessment and remediation

assessment_methods.description: Assess a lab enterprise wireless deployment with 802.1X/EAP authentication, identifying configuration weaknesses and credential exposure
Review enterprise wireless assessment reports for finding completeness, risk accuracy, and remediation quality

equipment: Alfa AWUS036ACH or equivalent monitor-mode-capable WiFi adapter
Managed access point for evil twin deployment
